title: MCP server (Python)
summary: A read-only MCP server on the official SDK (mcp 2.3): checked arguments, customer text marked untrusted, capped results, pinned tool descriptions, a chained audit file.
verified: RUN: the scaffold's 8 tests and its 8 contract cases ran here through a real MCP client in memory with mcp 2.3.0, including the argument checks, the untrusted envelope, the tool pins and the audit chain; the project audit reads READY. Not run against a live client session or over HTTP. 1.4.0: The cloud templates (qz cloud add) validated and planned for Azure, AWS, Google Cloud and Kubernetes in the Studio's CI with no cloud account; never applied.
stack_line: A read-only MCP server in Python (mcp 2.3).
live: No model and no key: connect a client with claude mcp add orders -- uv run --project . -m server.app
next: Replace orders() in server/data.py with a read-only call to your order system.
Change a tool, then run uv run -m server.pin and commit tests/tool_pins.json with it.
Before serving a team over HTTP, put OAuth in front of it (the SDK's token_verifier and AuthSettings).

ai_act.purpose: Gives AI agents read access to orders, and a refund tool that waits for a person's approval, over the Model Context Protocol.

open_line: No model and no vendor SDK: the server is plain Python on the open MCP standard.
cost_line: it calls no model, so there is no token spend to cut; `python3 .claude/qz/scripts/qz.py cost` reads not applicable on all six.

agent.none: a tool server: other agents run the loop and call it

model.none: it serves data to agents and calls no model itself

prompts.none: it calls no model; its tool descriptions are pinned in server/pin.py

sso.none: an MCP server over stdio: the person's own MCP client starts it and nothing listens on the network

rbac.none: every tool is read-only (readOnlyHint) and one person's client calls it over stdio: no write to separate

residency.none: it calls no host: it reads its own data and answers over stdio

network.none: it calls no host: it reads its own data and answers over stdio

endpoints.processor: none: it runs where the client runs
